title: Spectral Signatures of Valid Mathematical Reasoning
one_line_claim: Spectral properties of attention graphs (Fiedler value, HFER, entropy, smoothness) distinguish valid from invalid mathematical reasoning without training.
method_summary: Treat attention matrices as weighted graphs over tokens; extract four spectral diagnostics (Fiedler value, high-frequency energy ratio, spectral entropy, graph signal smoothness) from the Laplacian eigendecomposition. Classify validity with a single threshold on the selected metric at the best layer.

key_findings.finding: Cross-architecture validity detection with large effect sizes on seven models
key_findings.quote: Experiments across seven transformer models from four independent families (Meta, Alibaba, Microsoft, Mistral AI), with effect sizes |d| >= 2.09 and p_MW < 10^-47 in all cases

key_findings.finding: Achieves 85-95.6% classification accuracy with calibrated thresholds reaching 93-95% on full dataset
key_findings.quote: 85.0--95.6% classification accuracy under nested cross-validation and up to 95.6% with calibrated thresholds

key_findings.finding: Sliding Window Attention in Mistral-7B shifts discriminative signal from HFER to late-layer smoothness
key_findings.quote: Mistral-7B's Sliding Window Attention shifts the discriminative signal from HFER to late-layer Smoothness (d = 2.09, p_MW = 1.16 x 10^-48)

relation_to_herald.shared: Both detect failure modes in neural language models via internal signals without ground-truth failure labels; both analyze per-layer or per-token representations to classify output quality.
differs_on: Spectral reasons about formal mathematical correctness via attention graph geometry; HERALD predicts KV-cache compression-induced catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination) via per-token logit time series.
Spectral is training-free threshold classification on spectral metrics; HERALD trains an XGBoost predictor on engineered features with a horizon parameter for early warning.
Spectral evaluates on theorem-proof correctness (Lean); HERALD targets instruction-following and arithmetic (GSM8K) under compression stress.
